question: What will the BIST 100 index closing level be on October 16, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Random walk from the Oct 2 close of 12,270 over 10 trading days, with a small upward drift for nominal-lira inflation and post-crash mean reversion. September was the worst month since 2008 (-16.65%): funds short of cash had to sell, SPK ordered 131 funds liquidated, and a circuit breaker halted trading Sept 16. Realized volatility is very high, so the tails are wide. Downside risk: fund liquidations restart. Upside: support from the central bank and SPK plus a relief rally. calls.reasoning: Random walk anchored on the Oct 2 close of 12,270.18, with 10 trading sessions to the Oct 16 close and no holidays in the window. The index is in a bear market after September's -16.65% fund-redemption crisis. The SPK's interim-payment relief and central-bank liquidity support drove a rebound on Oct 1. Small nominal-lira inflation drift is offset by crisis overhang, giving a median of about 12,310. The Sept CPI release falls inside the window and the Oct 22 MPC falls after it. Tails are fat: renewed liquidation selling on the downside, a relief rally on the upside. No human prediction market or bookmaker found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the last close (12,270.18 on Oct 2), 10 remaining sessions, no holidays, the fund-crisis cause and that no market exists. The only factual gap is the MPC date: Run 3 places it on Oct 22, after resolution, and the other runs did not find it. Either way it doesn't bear on the window. The real disagreement is judgment about volatility (10-90 widths of 1,730 to 2,100). The Oct 2 session was calmer (+0.17%, ~1% intraday range), but post-crash volatility stays elevated. So I take daily vol of about 1.9%, between the normal and crash regimes, for a width of ~1,940. The median carries forward the runs' shared random-walk-plus-small-drift view; I found no evidence to move it. Tails are 3% below 10,500 (a 14% drop needs a renewed crisis, which is more plausible than an equal rally) and 2% above 14,000.
